memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'And to you I give one more ridge of land than to your brothers, the ridge I took from the Amorites with my sword and my bow.'" — Gen 48:22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Jacob's final word to Joseph is a gift of land — a ridge, a portion, one more than his brothers received. It is a small, concrete thing, and it means everything, because it is land in Canaan. Jacob is dying in Egypt and giving away property in a country he does not currently possess.

That takes some faith. He is handing on a title deed to a promise.

The mention of sword and bow is unusual for Jacob, and the reference is not fully explained anywhere in Genesis. Some connect it with events at Shechem. We do not need to resolve it. What matters is the confidence of the giving: God said this land would belong to his descendants, so Jacob distributes it as though it already does.

Centuries later, Joseph's bones would be carried out of Egypt and buried at Shechem, in the plot of ground Jacob had bought there (Josh 24:32). The promise held.

This is what faith looks like at the end of a life — not the absence of unfinished business, but confidence that God finishes what He starts. We hand on what we have been promised, whether or not we have seen it yet.

Our inheritance is kept in heaven for us, and it cannot spoil or fade (1 Pet 1:4).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What promise of God are you holding that you have not yet seen fulfilled?
2. Does your confidence rest in what you can see, or in God's word?
3. What are you handing on to those who come after you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You finish what You start. Help me hold Your promises with confidence even when I cannot see them yet, and hand on faith to those who come after me. Amen.
